variants.name: context.WithCancel / WithTimeout with Done-channel checks
variants.idiom_name: ctx context.Context as first parameter + select on ctx.Done()
variants.implementation_notes: Go's cancellation token is context.Context: context.WithCancel/WithTimeout/WithDeadline derive a child whose Done channel is closed when the parent is cancelled, the timeout elapses or the returned cancel func is called, and every operation takes ctx as its first parameter and selects on ctx.Done() or returns ctx.Err(). There is deliberately no Cancel method on the receiving side - only the owner that derived the context has the cancel func, and defer cancel() releases the child and its timer on every path. Cancellation is safe for concurrent use and propagates to derived contexts, so a whole request tree stops when the request's context is cancelled.
pitfalls: ctx.Done() is nil for context.Background() and context.TODO(): a select on it blocks forever, so a root context where cancellation is expected silently disables the feature.
Not calling cancel leaks the child and its timer until the parent is cancelled; defer cancel() immediately after deriving (go vet's lostcancel check flags the common mistake).
Checking ctx.Err() only after a long CPU loop gives no cancellation latency - check inside the loop or pass ctx to every blocking call, which most of the standard library accepts.
Storing required parameters or mutable state in a context value instead of passing them explicitly hides dependencies; context is for cancellation, deadlines and request-scoped data only.

variants.name: Cause-aware and lifecycle-aware contexts
variants.implementation_notes: Modern Go keeps the same signal but adds information and lifecycle control: WithCancelCause and WithDeadlineCause/WithTimeoutCause record a reason that context.Cause returns after Done is closed, so callers can distinguish 'client disconnected' from 'deadline exceeded' without guessing. context.AfterFunc (Go 1.21) registers work to run when a context is cancelled - the replacement for ad-hoc goroutine-plus-select shutdown hooks - and context.WithoutCancel detaches a copy that deliberately survives the parent (cleanup or audit work that must finish). Use the cause-aware API wherever the reason drives behaviour; keep with plain WithCancel where cancellation is binary.
pitfalls: context.Cause is only meaningful after Done is closed: reading it earlier returns nil, and code that branches on a nil cause silently takes the wrong path.

WithoutCancel detaches the tree but keeps the values; using it for ordinary work disables the very propagation the pattern exists for - reserve it for cleanup and detached auditing with their own timeout.
AfterFunc callbacks run in their own goroutine and are not called synchronously with cancellation; they must be idempotent and must not assume ordering with the operations they observe.
